metadata.title: George Soros's Top Q2 2026 Move: Trimming Amazon.com Inc at a -2.16% Portfolio Impact

content.text:
Insights from the Legendary Investor's Latest 13F Filing Reveal Strategic Shifts in Technology and Utilities
George Soros (Trades, Portfolio), the legendary financier born in Budapest in 1930, recently submitted his 13F filing for the second quarter of 2026, offering a rare glimpse into the investment strategy of one of history's most successful money managers. As chair of Soros Fund Management LLC, Soros converted his famous Quantum Group of Funds hedge fund into a family investment office in 2011. His investment philosophy, rooted in the theory of "reflexivity," posits that financial markets are inherently chaotic, driven by emotional human behavior rather than purely logical calculations. By carefully studying the divergence between asset values and market prices, Soros has consistently identified unique opportunities throughout his storied career, including his legendary short of the British Pound in 1992.
Summary of New Buys: Super Micro Computer Leads Fresh Positions
George Soros (Trades, Portfolio) added a total of 87 new stocks to his portfolio during the second quarter of 2026, signaling fresh conviction in several emerging opportunities. The most significant addition was Super Micro Computer Inc (NASDAQ:SMCI), with 2,175,408 shares acquired, accounting for 1.69% of the portfolio and a total value of $111.47 million. This substantial new position reflects growing interest in the artificial intelligence and high-performance computing sector. The second largest addition was American Electric Power Co Inc (NASDAQ:AEP), consisting of 768,000 shares, representing approximately 1.6% of the portfolio with a total value of $105.07 million. The third largest addition was Nebius Group NV (NASDAQ:NBIS), with 310,000 shares, accounting for 1.3% of the portfolio and a total value of $85.61 million, indicating a strategic bet on the technology infrastructure space.
Key Position Increases: Entergy Corp and Digital Realty Trust See Major Boosts
George Soros (Trades, Portfolio) also increased stakes in a total of 47 existing holdings, demonstrating confidence in select portfolio companies. The most notable increase was in Entergy Corp (NYSE:ETR), with an additional 836,734 shares bringing the total to 913,912 shares. This adjustment represents a significant 1,084.16% increase in share count, a 1.46% impact on the current portfolio, and a total value of $104.97 million. The second largest increase was in Digital Realty Trust Inc (NYSE:DLR), with an additional 482,200 shares bringing the total to 539,618 shares. This represents a substantial 839.81% increase in share count, with a total value of $96.90 million. These moves highlight Soros's growing conviction in utility and data center infrastructure plays, sectors that benefit from the accelerating digital transformation and energy transition trends.
Summary of Sold Out: Sealed Air and Amicus Therapeutics Completely Exited
George Soros (Trades, Portfolio) completely exited 78 holdings during the second quarter of 2026, demonstrating a willingness to cut losses and reallocate capital toward more promising opportunities. The most significant exit was Sealed Air Corp (SEE), where Soros sold all 2,751,799 shares, resulting in a -1.57% impact on the portfolio. This complete liquidation suggests a loss of confidence in the packaging company's growth prospects. Additionally, Soros liquidated all 5,753,186 shares of Amicus Therapeutics Inc (FOLD), causing a -1.13% impact on the portfolio. These exits free up substantial capital that can be redeployed into the new positions and increased stakes highlighted above, reflecting a dynamic portfolio management approach consistent with Soros's adaptive investment philosophy.
Key Position Reduces: Amazon.com Inc Faces Significant Trimming
George Soros (Trades, Portfolio) also reduced positions in 73 stocks during the quarter, with the most significant change being in Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN). Soros reduced his Amazon position by 763,260 shares, resulting in a -39.23% decrease in shares and a -2.16% impact on the portfolio. The stock traded at an average price of $250.33 during the quarter and has returned -1.71% over the past 3 months and 13.79% year-to-date. This substantial reduction in one of the world's largest technology companies suggests a strategic rebalancing rather than a complete exit. Additionally, Soros reduced his Smurfit WestRock PLC (NYSE:SW) position by 1,007,438 shares, resulting in a -39.97% reduction in shares and a -0.55% impact on the portfolio. The stock traded at an average price of $41.27 during the quarter and has returned 25.61% over the past 3 months and 31.14% year-to-date, indicating profit-taking in a strong performer.
Portfolio Overview: Technology and Utilities Dominate Holdings
At the end of the second quarter of 2026, George Soros (Trades, Portfolio)'s portfolio included 252 stocks, with the top holdings concentrated in several key positions. The largest holding was Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN) at 4.28% of the portfolio, followed by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd (NYSE:TSM) at 3.79%, Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) at 3.24%, NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) at 3.24%, and Electronic Arts Inc (NASDAQ:EA) at 3.03%. Despite the significant reduction in Amazon shares, it remains the largest position, underscoring Soros's continued long-term conviction in the e-commerce and cloud computing giant. The portfolio's holdings are mainly concentrated across all 11 industries, including Technology, Utilities, Communication Services, Financial Services, Industrials, Consumer Cyclical, Healthcare, Real Estate, Basic Materials, Consumer Defensive, and Energy, demonstrating a well-diversified approach to risk management.
For value investors seeking to understand the thinking of one of the world's most successful financiers, this 13F filing provides valuable insights into how Soros navigates complex market conditions. His strategic moves into high-growth technology infrastructure companies while trimming positions in mega-cap technology stocks suggest a nuanced approach to portfolio management. The significant increases in utility and data center companies indicate a bet on the long-term structural trends of digitalization and electrification. As always, investors should remember that 13F filings represent historical positions and may not reflect current holdings, but they offer a valuable window into the investment thinking of legendary market participants like George Soros (Trades, Portfolio).
